t: The authority of the Board to make commitments to guarantee or to issue guarantees under this Act expires on December 31, 1983.

fable.w: This section only sets an expiration date for the Board's authority to issue guarantees. The tempting reading is that the word "Board" signals an advisory body with outside members, but nothing here provides for consultation, comment, hearings, rulemaking, or a right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. It is a sunset clause with no participation process.
fable.s: The authority of the Board to make commitments to guarantee or to issue guarantees under this Act expires on December 31, 1983.

opus.w: This is a sunset provision that ends the Board's authority to issue guarantees on a set date. It does not involve any party outside the federal government in a federal decision. Mentioning a Board and guarantees does not create participation: there is no comment period, hearing, consultation or right to sue.
opus.s: The authority of the Board to make commitments to guarantee or to issue guarantees under this Act expires on December 31, 1983.
opus.b: Someone might be tempted to read "the Board" as a body with outside members, or to treat "commitments to guarantee" as a process that involves outside parties. Neither reading holds up. The section only sets the date when the Board's guarantee authority ends. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.
